_about: No se puede tocar: the Museo de la Costa Maya. Two set-ups: Iván at the ticket desk (10 pictures: the welcome, the closing-soon twist, which tickets?, the student or residence card, the audio guide, its language, paying, the exhibition upstairs on the right, the tickets and map, enjoy your visit) and Don Arturo in the first gallery for the don't-touch twist (its own first picture, sticky: the conversation ends there). The Sunday twist shows as the residence card (res_card); the flash variant of Don Arturo's twist uses the same picture.

items.prompt: Iván, the ticket clerk at the Museo de la Costa Maya, stands behind the ticket desk about one third from the left, both hands resting on the desk beside a card terminal with a blank screen and a small stack of blank paper tickets. A small, friendly, slightly shy smile ("Buenos días. ¿Cuántos boletos?").

Change only his pose: he half turns and points with one finger at a round wall clock with plain tick marks and no numerals on the wall behind him on the left, looking back at the learner with an apologetic, slightly worried smile (the museum closes in forty-five minutes).
Change only his pose: he fans out three blank paper tickets in one hand, one cream, one pale green and one pale blue, and raises his eyebrows politely (adults, students or seniors?).

Change only his pose: he holds a small plastic ID card with a blank photo square and no words between his thumb and fingers, studying it closely, then glancing up with a polite nod (checking the student credential, or a resident's card on a Sunday).
Change only his pose: he holds up a black audio guide handset with a blank screen in one hand, a pair of headphones looped over his wrist, an encouraging smile ("¿Quiere una audioguía?").

Change only his pose: five audio guide handsets now lie in a row on the desk, each with a small round colored sticker (red, blue, green, yellow, white; no flags, no letters); one hand hovers over them and he raises his eyebrows (which language?).
Change only his pose: he turns the card terminal toward the learner across the desk with one hand, its screen blank, a polite smile.
Change only his pose: he points upward and toward the right side of the picture, toward the upper floor, looking that way with a pleased smile (the new exhibition, upstairs on the right).
Change only his pose: he hands two blank paper tickets and a folded museum map (only simple shapes on its cover) across the desk with both hands, smiling ("¿Algo más?").
Change only his pose: he gestures with an open hand toward the galleries behind him, a warm, slightly shy smile ("¡Que disfrute su visita!").

Don Arturo, the museum guard, stands in the first gallery beyond the ticket desk (now out of sight), about one third from the left, beside the carved Maya stela on its plinth, one hand raised palm out toward the learner, the other at his side. A serious face with a twinkle in his eyes ("¡Disculpe! No se puede tocar, por favor."). The learner stands close to the stela; clay vessels in glass cases and soft spotlights behind him.
